stem: Which of the following statements about otitis media with effusion (OME) is correct?

options.text: It is otherwise referred to as “glue ear”
It often results in a sensorineural hearing loss
It is associated with ear pain and inflammation
Insertion of grommets (ventilating tubes) is a suitable treatment option
Adding adenoidectomy to grommet insertion reduces the grommet reinsertion rate by >20%

explanation: OME is commonly called glue ear. It causes a conductive hearing problem from middle ear fluid, usually without acute pain or inflammation. Grommets may be used in selected children, but the other statements are not generally correct as written.
rationale: The original item was a multiple-answer question. It was rewritten as a single-best-answer item to preserve the core concept while ensuring one clearly correct option.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Otitis media with effusion is commonly known as glue ear.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. OME typically causes conductive, not sensorineural, hearing loss.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. OME is usually not an acute painful inflammatory condition.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. Grommets can be used in selected cases, but this item asks for the single best correct statement; A is the clearest universally correct statement.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect. Evidence for benefit from adding adenoidectomy is context-dependent and this statement is too specific to be the best general answer.
